gap: No blockquote rule at all: A draws a 4px #BFBFBF vertical rule at x=644 spanning the full 138px height of the quote, while B puts a lone '>' glyph on line 1 and leaves the gutter completely empty below it — B's second quote line sits at 674px with zero ink in the margin, typographically indistinguishable from body prose, so any quote longer than one line loses containment.
gapTheirs: Markers sit inside the text column instead of hanging in the margin, so the prose left edge lands on six different x positions — paragraph 673px, h1 text 724px, h2 text 776px, quote text 728px, list text 730px, ordered-item text 778px — a 1-to-3 character (52-105px) jump every time the block type changes; worst of all the blockquote's wrapped line snaps back 54px from 728 to 674, giving a ragged left edge inside a single quote. B holds every one of those at 673px.
verdict: A indents your sentences by the width of its own syntax: type '## ' and the heading slides 105px right of the paragraph above it, and a blockquote that wraps drops its second line 54px left of its first. That is not markup rendering, it is markup occupying the page — you write down a fenceposted left edge that moves under you. B hangs every marker into the margin and never lets a glyph of prose start anywhere but 673px, which is the whole job; it pays for it with an empty gutter under wrapped quotes and markers at #7A7A7A instead of A's quieter #9E9E9E. A missing rule is a gap you can add in an afternoon; a text column that jumps is the design.

states.name: dark
states.gap: No block-level cue for the blockquote: only an 18px-wide '>' on the first line, at 4.1:1 contrast (#7A7A7A on #F9F9F9); the wrapped second line at x=674 is pixel-identical to a plain paragraph, so the quote's extent is invisible. B draws a 3px rule at x=644 spanning the full block (y792-935) and holds its markers quieter at 3.0:1.
states.gapTheirs: The text column moves with the marker: body 673px, list/h1 text 721px, h2 text 743px, ordered-list text 747px - a 74px (2.5-character) spread, and inside one blockquote the first line starts at 721px while its own wrapped line starts at 676px, a 45px jog leftward. A hangs every marker in a gutter (# at 624, ## at 600, > at 627, - at 630, 1. at 602) and holds one text column at 673±2px, so typing '#' doesn't shove the line 48px sideways.
states.verdict: A keeps a single left edge no matter what you type; B makes the sentence you are writing slide right by 48-74px the moment a marker appears, and its blockquote can't even align its own two lines. B's caret is worse: 6x72px of #00B5FF, full line-pitch, the most saturated thing on the page, against A's 4x54px caret in the text ink itself. B's compensations - a 3px quote rule and markers a stop dimmer (3.0:1 vs 4.1:1) - are real but small change against a text column that won't stay put. Neither gives headings a size step: '# The Lighthouse' sits in the same 37px cap band and 72px line pitch as body copy, bold and nothing else, so skimming for structure is guesswork in both.
